title: Faster static SDF bake (tools/bake_sdf.cpp) with output identical where the AO reads it
additional_information:
`tools/bake_sdf.cpp` bakes a 128^3 clipped signed distance field (float32) from triangles. The AO shader only reads distances below 1.075 m, so trilinear samples read stored values below 1.33 m (reach plus one voxel diagonal). The judge requires every voxel whose value is below 1.33 m to be bit-identical to the original baker's output, and allows values above that only to be raised. Values below the band must never change.

Measured so far (Apple M1, 8 threads): the distance pass dominates the Archive (1,908 triangles, ~1.5M BVH queries, ~0.5 us each). On the dense 488k-triangle mesh, the BVH build was a third of the time before it was parallelised. Already in the seed: parallel BVH build with identical node layout, skipping the unused grid build, per-voxel Lipschitz culling from the block centre's exact distance, `--reach`, and one triangle per BVH leaf (Archive -21%, output identical).

Tried and rejected: seeding each query with the block centre's triangle (no gain); BVH leaves of 8 (slower); tie-breaking slack at the seed distance (12% more triangle tests, because box scenes have many equidistant triangles).

The rig shares its host with other work, so timings are noisy; each cell runs 3 times per block.
ideas: float32 BVH bounds and a 4-wide BVH with structure-of-arrays boxes; keep triangle distances in double, or prove float gives identical stored values
SAH or binned-SAH build instead of median split (fewer node visits per query)
Process voxels in z-columns or Morton order within a block so the previous-voxel seed is tighter
Hierarchical culling: 8^3 block, then 4^3 and 2^3 sub-blocks, using the same 1-Lipschitz bound
Faster triangle distance: precompute per-triangle edge vectors and reciprocal lengths
Parallelise the winding-number sign pass and the OBJ/box loading
